summary: The story of Hoover Dam, built in Black Canyon on the Colorado River during the Great Depression. It opens in the 1931 heat of the canyon and the river that flooded and starved the farms below, follows the jobless men who camped in Ragtown and the new Boulder City near Las Vegas, Six Companies and superintendent Frank Crowe, then the four diversion tunnels that turned the river in 1932, the pouring of millions of cubic yards of concrete in cooled blocks, and the finish two years ahead of schedule in 1936. It ends with Lake Mead rising behind the 726 foot dam and power flowing to Nevada, Arizona and California.
